results.title: Istiqlal Party Intensifies Independence Campaign
results.note: Istiqlal founded 1944, escalated campaign from 1944 onward; 1950 activism well documented.

results.title: Sultan Mohammed V Reaffirms National Identity
results.note: Mohammed V's alignment with nationalism from 1950 is historically established.

results.title: Phosphate Production Expands Under French Control
results.note: OCP established 1920, Khouribga expansion and colonial labour disparity well documented.

results.title: French Pressure Forces Sultan to Condemn Nationalism
results.note: El Glaoui's role and French pressure on Mohammed V in 1951 confirmed by multiple sources.

results.title: Labour Unrest in Casablanca Docks
results.note: Union Marocaine du Travail founded 1955, not early 1950s. Dock strikes plausible but specific 1951 event unconfirmed.

results.title: Casablanca Riots Following Tunisian Union Leader's Murder
results.note: Farhat Hached assassinated 5 Dec 1952; Casablanca riots 7-8 Dec 1952 confirmed. Event spells name 'Ferhat' (alternate transliteration, not a factual error).

results.title: Istiqlal Party Banned by French Authorities
results.note: Crackdown and arrests after December 1952 riots confirmed.

results.title: Sultan Mohammed V Deposed and Exiled to Madagascar
results.note: Deposed 20 August 1953 (Eid al-Adha), exiled to Corsica then Madagascar; Moulay Arafa installed. All details confirmed.

results.title: Guerrilla Resistance Begins Against French Rule
results.note: Army of Liberation organised after 1953 exile; Rif-based insurgency confirmed.

results.title: Army of Liberation Escalates Operations
results.note: Dien Bien Phu May 1954, Algerian War Nov 1954; escalation of Moroccan resistance confirmed.

results.title: International Pressure Mounts on France Over Morocco
results.note: UN General Assembly discussion and Arab League support for Moroccan independence 1954 confirmed.

results.title: Mohammed V Returns from Exile
results.note: Returned 16 November 1955; event says 'October 1955' for French agreement — actually agreed late October, return November. Minor imprecision, core fact correct.

results.title: Morocco Gains Independence from France
results.note: Franco-Moroccan Declaration signed 2 March 1956; 44-year protectorate (1912-1956) confirmed.

results.title: Spain Relinquishes Northern Protectorate
results.note: Spain ceded northern zone April 1956; Tangier incorporated later 1956; Ceuta and Melilla retained. Confirmed.

results.title: Royal Armed Forces Established
results.note: Forces Armees Royales established 1956 merging Army of Liberation with former colonial soldiers. Confirmed.

results.title: Mohammed V Assumes Title of King
results.note: Mohammed V took title of King August 1957; Alaoui dynasty context confirmed.

results.title: First Post-Independence Government Formed
results.note: Mbarek Bekkai as first PM confirmed; Istiqlal-palace tensions documented.

results.title: Rif Uprising Suppressed by Royal Army
results.note: 1958-59 Rif uprising suppressed by Crown Prince Hassan; casualties confirmed.

results.title: Istiqlal Party Splits
results.note: Istiqlal split 1958-59; UNFP formed under Ben Barka confirmed.

results.title: National Union of Popular Forces Founded
results.note: UNFP formally established 1959 by Ben Barka after Istiqlal split. Confirmed.

results.title: Agadir Earthquake Devastates City
results.note: 29 February 1960, Mw 5.8, 12,000-15,000 deaths (approx one-third of city population). All details confirmed.

results.title: Hassan II Ascends the Throne
results.note: Mohammed V died 26 February 1961; Hassan II acceded same day, formally enthroned 3 March 1961. Event date '3 March 1961' is the enthronement date — accurate.

results.title: First Constitution Approved by Referendum
results.note: First constitution approved by referendum December 1962; Islam as state religion; bicameral parliament confirmed.

results.title: Security Services Launch Systematic Surveillance of Opposition
results.note: Surveillance of UNFP and left-wing groups by DST is historically established but no specific 1962 launch confirmed.

results.title: First Parliamentary Elections Held
results.note: May 1963 parliamentary elections, royalist majority, fraud allegations by Istiqlal and UNFP confirmed.

results.title: UNFP Leaders Arrested on Coup Conspiracy Charges
results.note: July 1963 mass arrests of UNFP on coup charges; death sentences later commuted; Ben Barka convicted in absentia. Confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Signs Association Agreement with EEC
results.note: Morocco-EEC association agreement 1969 (not 1964 — the 1964 date requires checking). Search confirms first formal agreement signed 1969; a 1964 agreement is documented in some sources.

results.title: Casablanca Student Protests and March Uprising
results.note: March 22-23 1965, started at Lycee Mohammed-V, education decree trigger confirmed. Death toll contested (dozens to 1000+).

results.title: Hassan II Declares State of Emergency and Dissolves Parliament
results.note: State of emergency June 1965, constitution suspended, direct royal rule until 1970. Confirmed.

results.title: Mehdi Ben Barka Kidnapped and Murdered in Paris
results.note: Abducted 29 October 1965 outside Brasserie Lipp, Paris. Oufkir implicated as orchestrator. Body never recovered. All details confirmed.

results.title: Student Movements and Political Unrest
results.note: 1968 student unrest at Mohammed V University in context of global 1968 wave confirmed.

results.title: Ifni Returned by Spain
results.note: Spain ceded Ifni to Morocco June 1969. Confirmed.

results.title: Rabat Summit of Arab League Held
results.note: 1969 Rabat Arab summit confirming Palestinian rights documented; Hassan II's hosting role confirmed.

results.title: New Constitution Restores Formal Parliamentary System
results.note: 1970 constitution ended 1965 state of emergency; opposition boycott confirmed.

results.title: Five Year Development Plan Launched
results.note: Five-year development plans existed in Morocco but specific 1970 plan details not independently confirmed.

results.title: Failed Military Coup at Skhirat Palace
results.note: 10 July 1971, ~1,400 cadets led by Medbouh stormed Skhirat. 278 total deaths including 98 civilian guests. Event says 'over 100 guests' — slightly understates but not FALSE.

results.title: F-5 Jets Attempt to Shoot Down Royal Aircraft
results.note: 16 August 1972, four F-5s attacked Boeing 727. Hassan used radio ruse. Oufkir died same day (officially suicide). Event says 'pretending to be a co-pilot' — actually Hassan himself grabbed radio, minor simplification, core fact correct.

results.title: Oufkir Family Imprisoned Without Trial
results.note: Oufkir family imprisoned 1972, released 1991; Malika Oufkir memoir 'Stolen Lives' confirmed.

results.title: Phosphate Prices Surge After Oil Crisis
results.note: Phosphate price surge post-1973 oil crisis; fivefold revenue increase widely documented.

results.title: Moroccanisation Policy Launches
results.note: Moroccanisation (Moroccanization) policy 1973 requiring majority Moroccan ownership confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Stakes Claim to Western Sahara
results.note: Morocco's formal claim to Spanish Sahara in 1974-1975 context; Polisario founded 1973 confirmed.

results.title: University Student Protests Intensify
results.note: Student protests mid-1970s plausible and consistent with record but no specific 1974 event confirmed.

results.title: International Court of Justice Delivers Ambiguous Western Sahara Opinion
results.note: ICJ advisory opinion October 1975 on Western Sahara confirmed; ambiguous findings on sovereignty vs. self-determination confirmed.

results.title: Green March — 350,000 Civilians Enter Western Sahara
results.note: 6 November 1975; ~350,000 unarmed Moroccans; Madrid Accords November 1975. All details confirmed.

results.title: Polisario Front Declares Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic
results.note: SADR proclaimed 27 February 1976, day after Spanish withdrawal. Algeria support and Tindouf base confirmed.

results.title: Tindouf Sahrawi Refugee Camps Established
results.note: Tindouf refugee camps established 1975-76; UNHCR/Algeria support; prolonged displacement confirmed.

results.title: First Parliamentary Elections Since 1963
results.note: June 1977 elections; royalist majority; Istiqlal and USFP performance confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Sends Troops to Zaire
results.note: Morocco deployed troops to Zaire 1977 to repel Katangan rebels; US/French logistical support confirmed.

results.title: Mauritania Abandons Western Sahara Claim
results.note: Event dated 1978 but peace treaty signed August 1979. Mauritania renounced claim 1979; Morocco annexed Tiris al-Gharbiyya immediately. Year in event file is slightly off (1978 vs 1979), core facts correct.

results.title: Economic Crisis as Phosphate Prices Collapse
results.note: Phosphate price collapse late 1970s, budget crisis and external debt confirmed.

results.title: Polisario Attacks Accelerate Mauritanian Withdrawal
results.note: Polisario raids on Zouerate iron ore infrastructure and Nouadhibou railway 1977-79 confirmed; contributed to Mauritanian peace treaty August 1979.

results.title: Derb Moulay Cherif Secret Prison in Operation
results.note: Derb Moulay Cherif secret detention and torture facility in Casablanca confirmed by IER report and human rights organisations.

results.title: Hassan II Promotes Islamic Legitimacy
results.note: Post-1979 Islamic legitimacy strategy; Commander of the Faithful role; Sufi brotherhoods as counterweights documented.

results.title: Casablanca Bread Riots — Hundreds Killed
results.note: June 1981 riots over food price increases; official toll 66; independent estimates higher. Casablanca as epicentre confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Agrees to Western Sahara Referendum in Principle
results.note: Hassan II's 1981 OAU announcement accepting referendum in principle confirmed; OAU admitted SADR 1984 prompting Morocco withdrawal.

results.title: IMF Structural Adjustment Programme Begins
results.note: IMF structural adjustment from early 1980s; subsidy cuts, dirham devaluation, trade liberalisation confirmed.

results.title: Moroccan Diaspora Remittances Become Economic Lifeline
results.note: Remittances as major foreign exchange source from early 1980s; ~1.5M workers abroad figure plausible and consistent with record.

results.title: Saharan Sand Wall Completed
results.note: Moroccan Wall/berm ~2,720 km; construction through early 1980s; landmines and sensors confirmed.

results.title: Drought Compounds Structural Adjustment Crisis
results.note: 1983 drought coinciding with IMF adjustment confirmed; rural-urban migration acceleration documented.

results.title: Fez Riots — Second Wave of Bread Riots
results.note: January 1984 riots in Fez, Nador, Tetouan, Al Hoceima triggered by subsidy cuts. Rif-region focus confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Withdraws from Organisation of African Unity
results.note: Morocco withdrew from OAU November 1984 after SADR admitted. Readmitted to AU 2017. Confirmed.

results.title: Amnesty International Reports on Moroccan Political Prisoners
results.note: Amnesty International documented torture and enforced disappearances in Morocco through 1980s; major reports published. Confirmed.

results.title: OCP Expands Phosphate Processing Toward Fertilisers
results.note: OCP phosphoric acid and fertiliser processing expansion at Safi and Jorf Lasfar confirmed.

results.title: Hassan II Hosts Secret Talks with Israeli Prime Minister
results.note: Secret meeting with Shimon Peres in July 1986; Morocco's back-channel Israel role confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Applies to Join European Community
results.note: Morocco formally applied to EC July 1987; rejected on geographic grounds confirmed.

results.title: Economic Liberalisation Reforms Deepen
results.note: Mid-to-late 1980s privatisation, export processing zones, FDI growth under IMF/World Bank guidance confirmed.

results.title: Morocco and Algeria Restore Diplomatic Relations
results.note: Morocco-Algeria diplomatic normalisation May 1988; AMU creation 1989 context confirmed.

results.title: Tangier Free Zone Established as Export Platform
results.note: Tangier Free Zone formally established 1992 (not late 1980s); concept may have been discussed earlier but specific 1988 founding not confirmed.

results.title: Arab Maghreb Union Founded
results.note: AMU Treaty of Marrakech February 1989; five founding states confirmed; subsequent inactivity documented.

results.title: Human Rights Council Established
results.note: CCDH (Consultative Council on Human Rights) established 1990 by Hassan II confirmed.

results.title: Gulf War — Morocco Joins Coalition
results.note: Morocco deployed ~1,700 troops to Gulf War coalition 1990-91 confirmed.

results.title: UN-Brokered Ceasefire in Western Sahara
results.note: UN ceasefire September 1991; MINURSO created; referendum repeatedly postponed confirmed.

results.title: Oufkir Family Released After 20 Years
results.note: Oufkir family released 1991 after ~19 years detention; Malika Oufkir memoir confirmed.

results.title: New Constitution Approved with Rights Provisions
results.note: 1992 constitutional revision with human rights provisions confirmed.

results.title: Severe Drought Devastates Agriculture
results.note: 1992 drought reducing cereal output; food imports and rural-urban migration confirmed.

results.title: First Women Elected to Moroccan Parliament
results.note: Two women elected to parliament in 1993 elections confirmed.

results.title: Algeria Closes Border with Morocco
results.note: Event year 1993 but actual border closure August 1994 (following Marrakech attack). Year in file is off by one; core fact correct.

results.title: Marrakech Terrorist Attack and Atlas Asni Hotel Bombing
results.note: August 1994 Atlas Asni Hotel attack killing two Spanish tourists; Algerian militant connections; border closure consequence confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Joins World Trade Organisation at Founding
results.note: Morocco was founding WTO member January 1995 confirmed.

results.title: Constitutional Reform Creates Bicameral Parliament
results.note: 1996 bicameral parliament reform; Chamber of Counsellors added; alternance elections context confirmed.

results.title: Alternance — Opposition Leader Becomes Prime Minister
results.note: Youssoufi appointed PM February 1998 after 1997 elections; first alternance in Moroccan history confirmed.

results.title: Equity and Reconciliation Commission Precursors Established
results.note: 1998 Youssoufi government steps toward transitional justice; IER precursor bodies confirmed.

results.title: Tanger Med Port Concept Takes Shape
results.note: Tanger Med feasibility studies dated to late 1990s is plausible but specific 1998 planning phase not independently confirmed.

results.title: Hassan II Dies — Mohammed VI Ascends Throne
results.note: Hassan II died 23 July 1999; Mohammed VI proclaimed same day; Basri dismissed shortly after. All confirmed.

results.title: Driss Basri Dismissed by Mohammed VI
results.note: Basri dismissed as interior minister by Mohammed VI shortly after accession; served as interior minister since 1979 confirmed.

results.title: One Million March in Casablanca Against Women's Rights Plan
results.note: March 2000 Casablanca conservative march against women's plan; Rabat counter-demonstration confirmed.

results.title: Mohammed VI Visits Western Sahara
results.note: Mohammed VI's 2001 visit to Western Sahara — first by Moroccan monarch — confirmed.

results.title: Mohammed VI Launches Rural Poverty Reduction Strategy
results.note: 2001 rural poverty strategy; INDH formally launched 2005 as successor; trajectory confirmed.

results.title: Morocco-Spain Confrontation at Parsley Island
results.note: July 2002 Parsley Island incident; Moroccan soldiers raised flag; Spanish Operation Romeo Sierra; US mediation confirmed.

results.title: Parliamentary Elections — Moderate Islamists Make Gains
results.note: September 2002 elections; PJD third-largest party; considered fairest elections to that point confirmed.

results.title: Casablanca Bombings Kill 45 People
results.note: 16 May 2003; 12 coordinated suicide bombers; 45 total deaths (33 victims + 12 bombers); 100+ injured; Salafia Jihadia confirmed.

results.title: Anti-Terrorism Law Enacted
results.note: Anti-terrorism law enacted weeks after May 2003 bombings; HRW criticism of broad powers confirmed.

results.title: Moudawwana Family Law Reformed — Major Women's Rights Advance
results.note: February 2004 Moudawwana reforms; minimum marriage age raised, divorce equalised, polygamy restricted; Mohammed VI's personal endorsement confirmed.

results.title: Equity and Reconciliation Commission Established
results.note: IER established January 2004; chaired by Benzekri (former political prisoner); first Arab world truth commission; 16,000+ claims confirmed.

results.title: IER Delivers Final Report with Reparations Recommendations
results.note: IER final report November 2005; 742 disappearances documented; reparations to ~16,000 families confirmed.

results.title: Sub-Saharan Migration Crisis at Ceuta and Melilla
results.note: September-October 2005 fence-storming attempts; at least 14 migrants killed; deportations to Algeria/Mauritania borders confirmed.

results.title: National Initiative for Human Development Launched
results.note: INDH launched May 2005 (event file says 2006 but description correctly states 2005). Year in file is off by one; core facts correct.

results.title: Parliamentary Elections — Low Turnout Signals Disengagement
results.note: September 2007 elections; ~37% turnout record low; Istiqlal largest party; Abbas El Fassi as PM confirmed.

results.title: US-Morocco Free Trade Agreement Deepens Trade Ties
results.note: US-Morocco FTA entered into force 2006; 2007 deeper implementation phase confirmed.

results.title: Boushtatat Bread Riots in Sefrou
results.note: Food price spike protests 2008 are documented in Morocco but specific Sefrou 'Boushtatat' riots not confirmed by available sources.

results.title: Advanced Status Agreement with European Union
results.note: Morocco EU Advanced Status formalised October 2008 confirmed.

results.title: Nador Migrant Detention and Deportation Controversy
results.note: MSF and HRW documented systematic deportations of sub-Saharan migrants including UNHCR-registered asylum seekers in 2008-09 confirmed.

results.title: Phosphate Prices Recover — OCP Expands
results.note: Post-2008 phosphate price recovery; OCP Africa investment strategy and ~70% global reserve share confirmed.

results.title: WikiLeaks Cables Reveal Royal Family Business Interests
results.note: 2010 WikiLeaks cables including Rabat embassy assessments of 'predatory elites' confirmed.

results.title: Solar Energy Megaproject Launched
results.note: Morocco Solar Plan announced 2009-2010; 2,000 MW target by 2020; Noor Ouarzazate as flagship confirmed.

results.title: February 20 Movement Demands Constitutional Reform
results.note: February 20 Movement launched 20 February 2011; tens of thousands in Casablanca, Rabat; diverse coalition confirmed.

results.title: Mohammed VI Announces Constitutional Reform in Response to Protests
results.note: Royal speech 9 March 2011 announcing constitutional revision; Amazigh recognition; confirmed.

results.title: New Constitution Approved by Referendum
results.note: 1 July 2011 referendum; 98.49% yes; Tamazight as official language; Feb 20 Movement boycott confirmed.

results.title: PJD Wins Parliamentary Elections
results.note: November 2011 elections; PJD largest party; Benkirane appointed first Islamist head of government confirmed.

results.title: Hirak Rif Movement Precursors in North
results.note: Structural grievances in Rif region well documented but specific 2012 fish vendor protests as named precursor events not confirmed.

results.title: Noor Ouarzazate Solar Plant Construction Begins
results.note: Ground broken on Noor Ouarzazate 2012; $2.5B+ total investment; international development bank financing confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Strengthens Africa Investment Strategy
results.note: Attijariwafa, Banque Populaire Africa expansion; Royal Air Maroc African routes; Mohammed VI royal tours confirmed.

results.title: Casablanca Finance City Develops as Regional Hub
results.note: CFC established 2010; growth as regional hub from 2013-14 with international firms confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Positions for COP22 Climate Hosting Role
results.note: COP22 held in Marrakech November 2016; Morocco's campaign to host confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Passes Law Recognising Tamazight Language Rights
results.note: Organic law for Tamazight implementation post-2011 constitution; IRCAM expanded mandate confirmed.

results.title: Hirak Rif Movement Erupts Following Fish Vendor Death
results.note: Mouhcine Fikri crushed in garbage truck October 2016; Nasser Zefzafi as leader; Al Hoceima protests confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Rejoins African Union After 33 Years
results.note: Morocco applied July 2016; readmitted January 2017 after 33-year absence. Event year 2016 (application year) is accurate.

results.title: Hirak Rif Leaders Arrested and Sentenced
results.note: Zefzafi arrested May 2017; sentenced June 2018 to 20 years. Event year 2017 covers arrests; sentencing 2018. Core facts correct.

results.title: Morocco-Spain Agreement on Migration Management
results.note: 2018 Morocco-Spain migration cooperation agreements; EU pressure and Moroccan leverage confirmed.

results.title: Boycott Movement Targets Consumer Goods Companies
results.note: April 2018 boycott of Centrale Danone, Afriquia, Sidi Ali; social media organised; significant sales impact confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Hosts Interreligious Summit
results.note: Marrakesh Declaration January 2019; Muslim scholars on religious minority rights; Mohammed VI's moderate Islam positioning confirmed.

results.title: COVID-19 Pandemic — Morocco Responds Rapidly
results.note: Health emergency 20 March 2020; strict lockdown with movement permits; COVID-19 Special Fund; domestic mask production confirmed.

results.title: Morocco-Israel Normalisation Agreement
results.note: Normalisation announced 10 December 2020; Abraham Accords; US Western Sahara recognition as quid pro quo confirmed.

results.title: US Recognises Moroccan Sovereignty Over Western Sahara
results.note: Presidential Proclamation 10 December 2020; no major power followed; Polisario resumed operations; UN position unchanged. Confirmed.

results.title: Morocco-Spain Crisis Over Ceuta and Western Sahara
results.note: May 2021 ~10,000 migrants entered Ceuta in one day; linked to Spain hosting Polisario leader Brahim Ghali; Spain's subsequent 2022 position shift confirmed.

results.title: Vaccination Campaign Achieves Strong Coverage
results.note: Morocco launched vaccination January 2021; among highest rates in Africa; Mohammed VI received vaccine publicly confirmed.

results.title: Spain Backs Moroccan Autonomy Plan for Western Sahara
results.note: Spain endorsed Morocco's autonomy plan March 2022; Algeria recalled ambassador from Spain; confirmed.

results.title: FIFA 2030 World Cup Bid — Spain-Morocco-Portugal Co-Host
results.note: Spain-Morocco-Portugal awarded 2030 co-hosting; Morocco to host significant share of matches confirmed.

results.title: Noor Solar Complex Reaches Major Capacity Milestone
results.note: Noor complex 580 MW capacity; Tarfaya wind farm; 52% renewable by 2030 target confirmed.

results.title: Al Haouz Earthquake Kills 3,000 People
results.note: 8 September 2023, M6.8, 2,960 confirmed deaths (event says 'nearly 3,000'). High Atlas epicentre; international rescue teams confirmed.

results.title: Morocco World Cup Qatar — Historic Semi-Final Run
results.note: Morocco reached World Cup semi-finals at Qatar 2022 (held Nov-Dec 2022); first African/Arab nation to do so. Event year 2023 but tournament was 2022 — minor year mislabelling.

results.title: Earthquake Reconstruction Programme Launched
results.note: Mohammed VI announced 120 billion dirham reconstruction programme over 5 years following earthquake. Confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Advances 2030 World Cup Infrastructure
results.note: 2030 World Cup infrastructure investment across Casablanca, Rabat, Tangier, Agadir, Marrakech, Fez confirmed.

results.title: Phosphate Diplomacy Deepens Africa Engagement
results.note: OCP Africa fertiliser agreements and African Fertilizer Summit role confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Signs Green Hydrogen Agreement with Europe
results.note: Morocco-Germany and EU green hydrogen framework agreements 2023-24; pilot projects confirmed.

results.title: Morocco Hosts Africa Cup of Nations Successfully
results.note: Morocco hosted AFCON January-February 2025 confirmed.

results.title: Hirak Rif Political Prisoner Releases Debated
results.note: Zefzafi and other Hirak prisoners still imprisoned 2025; ongoing international pressure confirmed.

results.title: Morocco's Economy Grows — Services and Manufacturing Diversify
results.note: Tanger Med as Africa's largest container port; automotive and aerospace diversification; GDP per capita growth since 2000 confirmed.

results.title: Western Sahara Autonomy Plan Gains Additional International Recognition
results.note: Continued UN Staffan de Mistura shuttle diplomacy; autonomy plan gaining European/African endorsements while Polisario maintains referendum demand confirmed.
